Note::json_escape¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::json_escape() const

Escape A String For A JSON String Body¶

json_escape() rewrites each cell so its characters are legal between the quotes of a JSON string. It applies the escapes the JSON grammar requires and nothing more:

Input

Output

"

\"

\

\\

U+0008 backspace

\b

U+000C form feed

\f

U+000A line feed

\n

U+000D carriage return

\r

U+0009 tab

\t

any other control U+0000–U+001F

\u00XX (lower-case hex)

Every byte from 0x20 up is copied through unchanged. In particular the result is still UTF-8 — a non-ASCII character such as é is not turned into \uXXXX — and / is left as-is; both are valid in JSON.

json_escape() produces the contents of a JSON string. It does not add the surrounding " quotes, and there is no json_unescape inverse. Feed the result into a serializer, or wrap it in quotes yourself. The operation preserves shape, keeps the input’s encoding tag, and returns a fresh Note.

Printing the result¶

The Note printer escapes \ and " for its own display, which would show the backslashes this method just added as \\. The examples below print the raw bytes of each cell instead, so the output is exactly what json_escape() wrote:

for (std::int64_t i = 0; i < n.numel(); ++i)
  std::cout << std::string(n.at(i)) << "\n";

Example 1: Quotes And Backslashes¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note({std::string("say \"hi\" \\ end")}).json_escape();
for (std::int64_t i = 0; i < n.numel(); ++i)
  std::cout << std::string(n.at(i)) << "\n";

Output¶

say \"hi\" \\ end

Each " becomes \", and the lone \ becomes \\.

Example 2: Control Characters¶

const auto n =
    pluss::make_note({std::string("tab\t nl\n cr\r bell") + '\x07' + " end"}).json_escape();
for (std::int64_t i = 0; i < n.numel(); ++i)
  std::cout << std::string(n.at(i)) << "\n";

Output¶

tab\t nl\n cr\r bell\u0007 end

Tab, line feed, and carriage return get their short forms; the bell (U+0007) has no short form, so it becomes the six characters \u0007.

Example 3: Non-ASCII Passes Through¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note({"café"}).json_escape();
for (std::int64_t i = 0; i < n.numel(); ++i)
  std::cout << std::string(n.at(i)) << "\n";

Output¶

café
